Subject: Before you pack it away — a quick gear check
Preview: End-of-season maintenance keeps your kit ready for the next trip.
Body: The season's winding down. Before your gear goes into storage, it's worth spending an hour going through what came back from the field with you.

A few things worth checking on your tent specifically:

**Poles.** Wipe down aluminum or fiberglass sections and inspect for hairline cracks or bent segments. A compromised pole won't be obvious until you need it most.

**Seams and zippers.** Look for delaminating seam tape and test every zipper pull under load. Clean out grit with a soft brush before it grinds the coil.

**Rainfly and floor.** Ripstop nylon holds up well, but prolonged moisture in storage accelerates mildew and can degrade the DWR coating. If the fly was packed wet, re-pitch it in the yard and let it dry fully before folding.

**Stakes.** Count them. Stakes are the easiest piece of kit to lose mid-trip and the easiest to replace before next season.

Set the tent up one more time in the backyard. You'll catch anything you missed in the field, and you won't be sorting it out at the trailhead in April.

We'll have restocked gear and maintenance supplies available soon — check back for updates.
